description: Reads the local run history: one record per finished translate, watch, translation.translatePending or retranslation run that left a trace, failed and refused runs included, newest first, with when it ran, what triggered it (translate or retranslate), the provider and model, entries (for a retranslate record, how many entries were attempted), the tokens it used, what it cost, and per locale the counts of translated keys, cache hits, fuzzy hits, generated plural forms, pruned keys, integrity refusals and provider failures, plus how many keys were missing, stale or up to date afterwards. Use it to report spend and coverage over time, where usage.summary only reports the last run. Records hold counts only, never a key name or a text. cost is frozen when the run ended, from the rates the config held then: pricing priced carries currency, asOf and amount; no-rate-on-file, rate-unit-mismatch, no-usage (keys were sent but the provider reported no tokens) and not-billed (verbatra does not price the provider: a self-hosted openai-compatible or LibreTranslate server, or none; a hosted endpoint may still bill) carry no amount, so report them as no rate or unknown and never as free. A cost with basis source-characters is an estimate from the source characters sent to a machine-translation provider that reports no usage: say estimated, and mention its caveats; keys the provider failed on are not counted. A cost with the caveat USAGE_PARTIAL, priced, unpriced or not-billed, is a lower bound: a locale sent keys and reported no tokens, so say at least, never exactly, and read the tokens the same way (a locale that reported for only some of its sub-batches cannot be detected). A locale without coverage was not measured in that run. Dry runs and runs that left no trace are not recorded, and the file keeps the newest 1000 records. The optional limit says how many of the newest records to return: 50 by default and at most 200, a larger value is reduced to that. total counts every readable record, unreadableRecords the lines that could not be read and were left out, and unavailable is set when the whole file could not be read, so an empty records list is then not proof that no run happened. Read-only: it calls no provider and writes nothing.
name: usage.history
